pick_implementation.title: Pick the Tesla developer-app credential set
pick_implementation.description: Choose existing application credentials or add new ones. Add the same client_id / client_secret you registered for `tesla_fleet` — each integration goes through OAuth independently and gets its own refresh token, so they no longer rotate over each other.

region.title: Region
region.description: Tesla serves Fleet API accounts from regional endpoints. The region detected from your Tesla account is preselected — confirm it or correct it if needed.

vehicle.title: Select vehicle
vehicle.description: Choose the VIN this integration should track.

endpoint.title: Telemetry endpoint
endpoint.description:
Configure how Tesla reaches Home Assistant. The hostname must resolve publicly and present a TLS cert valid for the chain you'll put in `fleet_telemetry_config.ca`. The proxy secret is what nginx will inject as `X-Tesla-Proxy-Secret` on every forwarded request — copy it into your nginx config. It must be at least {min_secret_length} characters: it is all that authenticates the endpoint, which Home Assistant's own port also serves.

The partner private key is the EC P-256 (secp256r1) key whose public counterpart is hosted at `https://your-partner-domain/.well-known/appspecific/com.tesla.3p.public-key.pem`. If you don't have one yet, generate it with `openssl ecparam -genkey -name prime256v1 -noout -out partner.key` and paste the file contents below.

When adding another vehicle these fields are pre-filled from your existing setup — leave them unchanged unless your deployment moved.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Tesla
reauth_confirm.description: {name} needs a new Tesla authorization. This happens when “Allow vehicle commands” is on but the current authorization doesn't include the vehicle_cmds scope — continuing sends you to Tesla to grant it. Nothing else about the entry changes.

error.weak_proxy_secret: The proxy secret must be at least {min_secret_length} characters. It is the only thing that authenticates the telemetry endpoint, so keep the generated one unless you have a stronger one.

init.title: Telemetry signals
init.description: Configure which signals the vehicle streams and how often. Each value is the minimum seconds between updates for that signal — Tesla emits on change and no more than once per interval, so it's a ceiling for high-churn signals, not a poll. Set a signal to 0 to disable it. Saving re-pushes the config to the car (no bootstrap needed). Leaving everything untouched keeps the built-in defaults.

driving.name: Driving & navigation
driving.description: Location, speed, gear, active-route and FSD-distance signals. 0 disables a signal.

battery.name: Battery & range
battery.description: State of charge and range estimates. 0 disables a signal.

charging.name: Charging
charging.description: Charge state, power/energy, cable, and limit signals. 0 disables a signal.

climate.name: Climate & cabin
climate.description: Cabin/outside temperature and HVAC signals. 0 disables a signal.

body.name: Body & security
body.description: Doors, windows, lock, and seat-occupancy signals. 0 disables a signal.

software.name: Software update
software.description: Update version and download/install progress. 0 disables a signal.

powertrain.name: Powertrain & thermal
powertrain.description: Drive-unit and battery-module temperatures. 0 disables a signal.

additional.name: Additional signals
additional.description: Signals you've added from the full catalog. 0 removes a signal.

add_signals.name: Add signals from the full Tesla catalog
add_signals.description: Pick any signal from the complete Tesla catalog to start streaming it; it appears above with its own interval next time you open this dialog. Each added signal also gets a sensor named after it (numbers as measurements, everything else as text); setting it to 0 removes both the signal and its sensor. Every added signal counts toward your signal bill. Not every vehicle sends every signal — older cars may never report some, in which case the sensor stays unknown.

cost.name: Signal cost estimate
cost.description: Tesla bills per streaming signal (one per data point). This rate drives the ‘Estimated signal cost’ sensor only — it does not change what Tesla charges. The default (≈ 6.67 per million) mirrors Tesla's published US rate of roughly $1 per 150,000 signals.

vehicle_commands.name: Vehicle commands
vehicle_commands.description: Off by default: the integration only reads telemetry. Turning this on enables the navigate service (sends a destination to the car) and, if the current authorization lacks the vehicle_cmds scope, starts a re-authentication that asks Tesla for it. Works only on vehicles that accept unsigned Fleet API commands (pre-2021 Model S/X).

teslamate.name: TeslaMate bridge
teslamate.description: Off by default. Serves this vehicle's live stream to TeslaMate in the streaming protocol its TESLA_WSS_HOST expects, so the car streams once and both systems read it. Enabling it adds a WebSocket endpoint on Home Assistant's own HTTP server that does not use Home Assistant's login; it is gated by the proxy secret the vehicle endpoint already uses, so keep that endpoint on your LAN. Takes effect when the entry reloads.

bootstrap.name: Bootstrap (one-time onboarding)
bootstrap.description: Registers the partner domain with Tesla (if requested) and pushes the initial fleet telemetry config so the configured vehicle starts streaming. Run once after first install — afterwards, use `resync_telemetry_config` to refresh the config's `exp` field.

entry_id.description: Which Tesla Fleet Telemetry entry to act on. Required only when more than one is configured.

register_partner_domain.name: Register partner domain
register_partner_domain.description: Set to false if the partner app is already registered through another integration and you only need to push the telemetry config.

ca_pem.name: CA bundle override (PEM)
ca_pem.description: Override the default Let's Encrypt root bundle used as the vehicle's TLS trust anchor. Only set this if your hostname uses a non-LE CA.

resync_telemetry_config.name: Re-push telemetry config
resync_telemetry_config.description: Pushes the current `fleet_telemetry_config` again. The config's `exp` field is about 30 days; call this weekly via an automation so nothing lapses.

get_telemetry_config.name: Show current telemetry config
get_telemetry_config.description: Calls Tesla's `fleet_telemetry_config` endpoint and returns the response. Use this to check whether the vehicle has actually synced the config you pushed — look for `synced: true` in the response.

dump_public_key.name: Show partner public key
dump_public_key.description: Returns the EC P-256 public key derived from the configured private key, ready to host at the partner domain's `.well-known/appspecific/com.tesla.3p.public-key.pem` path. Returned via the action response and also written to the log.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Which Tesla Fleet Telemetry entry to act on. Required only when more than one is configured.

set_interval_preset.name: Set telemetry interval preset
set_interval_preset.description: Switches the per-field telemetry intervals to a named preset and re-pushes the telemetry config so the change takes effect. `default` is the steady-state config — a 5 s ceiling on location and speed, higher ceilings on slower-moving signals, and Tesla still pushes on change. `high_rate` drops `Location` and `VehicleSpeed` to about 1 s for live-trace use; every other signal keeps its configured interval, so switch back to `default` afterwards. The preset is persisted to the entry so it survives a restart.

navigate.name: Send a destination to the car
navigate.description: Sends a destination to the vehicle's navigation — either free text, which the car looks up itself exactly as when a location is shared from the Tesla phone app, or coordinates. Give one or the other. Off unless the integration's "Allow vehicle commands" option is on; also needs an awake car that accepts unsigned Fleet API commands (pre-2021 Model S/X).

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Which Tesla Fleet Telemetry entry to act on. Required only when more than one is configured.

destination.name: Destination
destination.description: An address, a place name, or "place, city". Leave empty when sending coordinates.

latitude.name: Latitude
latitude.description: Use with longitude instead of a text destination.

longitude.name: Longitude
longitude.description: Use with latitude instead of a text destination.

order.name: Trip order
order.description: Coordinates only. Lets the car decide, replaces the current trip, or adds the destination as the next or last stop.

locale.name: Locale
locale.description: Text destinations only: the locale the car reads the text in, as a BCP 47 tag.
